message: The acknowledgement watermark is the goal entity's updatedAt, which any write to the goal bumps - including the staff member's own edits in the NS calculator. After a user views the card, opens the wizard and saves a field, the card returns on the dashboard saying "Your goal changed since you last looked", which is false.

The GqlMockedProvider UserOption mock is not parameterized by the `key` variable, so it returns the same fixture ({key:"user_type_verified", value:"true"}) for both ConfirmUserGroupModal's check and NewStaffGoalReadyCard's own `new_staff_goal_acknowledged_goal-1` lookup. The test only passes because "true" happens to parse as an invalid Date (NaN), so it coincidentally looks unacknowledged rather than because the mock actually answers the right key.
No test covers a GraphQL error response for NewStaffGoalReady or UserOption, so a regression that leaves the card stuck loading/crashing on an Apollo error would go undetected.

The card forks the eligibility gate every other nsGoalCalculator entry point uses: it checks only DISABLE_NS_GOAL_CALCULATOR and inNsGoalCalcIneligibleGroup, omitting reportsDisabled and the userType check. The card and its link can therefore appear for users the nav hides the tool from, and for users the page itself answers with LimitedAccess.

SentGoalCard does `if (loading || ...) return null` on useUserOptionQuery, whose loading flag goes true again on every refetch under the app-wide cache-and-network + notifyOnNetworkStatusChange policy. This is the documented refetch-flash bug: an already-visible, undismissed card will vanish and reappear on refocus/cache invalidation, not just on first load.

acknowledge() has no error handling on updateUserOption, and no test exercises a rejected mutation; because dismissed is set to true unconditionally before the request resolves, a failed save leaves the card permanently hidden for that session with nothing asserting or fixing that behavior.

The acknowledgement timestamp is parsed with `new Date(string)` instead of Luxon, so a partially parseable non-ISO value (e.g. "2026" or "Sep 2026") reads as a valid acknowledgement in the past and silently flips the card to the "Your MPD goal was updated" copy. The repo convention is `DateTime.fromISO(...).isValid`, because `new Date(arbitraryString)` parsing is implementation-defined per spec.

`if (loading) return null` blanks the card on every refetch of the UserOption query, not just the first load, because the client sets `fetchPolicy: cache-and-network` with `notifyOnNetworkStatusChange: true` — so `loading` goes true again on each remount while cached `data` is already present. That reintroduces exactly the card flash the comment two lines above says this code exists to avoid.

`acknowledge()` sets `dismissed` to true and fires `updateUserOption` without awaiting or catching it, so a failed write produces an unhandled promise rejection and leaves the card hidden for the rest of the session while nothing was persisted — it silently returns on the next page load. The optimistic response is never rolled back into visible state.

New key "Your goal changed since you last looked..." is inserted after "Your MPD goal was updated" instead of before "Your MPD goal is ready", which is where crowdin/sort-translations.js (a.localeCompare(b)) would place it.

StaffMemberDrawer.tsx now renders the Employment Type row via transformAssignmentCategoryGroup(assignmentCategoryGroup, t) instead of the hardcoded pendingField placeholder, but StaffMemberDrawer.test.tsx has no assertion on this row for either a populated or null assignmentCategoryGroup. A regression that reverts this line to pendingField would not be caught by any test.

MpdAssignmentCategoryGroupEnum is mapped to display labels in two places: the new transformAssignmentCategoryGroup helper and the filter panel MenuItem children. The repo rule is one enum value maps to one label, so the dropdown and the row/drawer can drift apart on the next copy change.

transformAssignmentCategoryGroup already returns early for null/undefined, so the trailing default branch is unreachable for every value the type allows. It converts a future schema enum member from a compile error into a silent em dash in the UI.
dismissalDetail: the default branch is a deliberate runtime fallback for server enum values the client doesn't know yet; the unreachable-branch defect is gone (the early null return was removed) and helpers.test.ts covers the unknown-value path

message: The test is named "omits assignmentCategoryGroup" but it asserts the variable is sent as an explicit null, so it does not actually prove the argument is omitted.

Test is named 'omits assignmentCategoryGroup until an employment type is chosen' but the assertion checks that the variable is sent with value null, not that the key is omitted from the operation — the name and the behavior it verifies do not match.
The JSDoc comment on transformAssignmentCategoryGroup only restates the function name/signature and adds no non-obvious why, which this repo has repeatedly asked reviewers to trim.

The repo keeps localized enum-label helpers as getLocalizedX in src/lib/functions; this one is named transformAssignmentCategoryGroup and lives in a feature helpers file. Harmless today because the enum is used only here, but it makes the helper hard to find if a second feature needs the same label.

pendingField is documented as "Stands in for fields managedStaff cannot supply yet", but it is now also the placeholder for a field the API does supply as null. Grepping pendingField no longer tells you which fields are still unimplemented.

The MpdGoalAdmin gotcha note still says an empty cohort list means no cohorts exist at all, not that this user has none, and that the context auto-selects the first cohort whenever the list is non-empty. This PR makes coordinators see a role-filtered list (trainingSize > 0), so a coordinator can now get an empty list while cohorts do exist team-wide — the doc no longer matches the code it describes.

This adds a second empty state for the same situation the existing No Training Selected state (PR #2013) was built for, and they act differently: the new one hides the Training selector, the old one keeps it disabled. For coordinators the old branch can no longer be reached, so its comment is now stale, and admins with zero cohorts still get the old copy and layout.
noVisibleCohorts explicitly guards on !cohortsLoading and !cohortsError so the empty-state message does not flash during load or replace a real error, but no test in the diff exercises either guard.
Added inline comment restates what the ternary already shows (replacing CohortBar/ActiveGoalsContent with NullStateBox) rather than explaining a non-obvious why beyond the one useful clause.

The role check waits on userLoading but ignores a GetUser error. If that query fails, isGoalsAdmin comes back false, so an admin gets the coordinator-filtered list and may see a misleading message that cohorts do not include staff in their ministry.

The cohorts memo now filters non-admins to trainingSize > 0, but no test covers a coordinator whose selected cohort disappears from the filtered list after a re-render (e.g. attendees reassigned away mid-session), which is the scenario the useEffect's stale-selection fallback exists for.

Gating the cohort list on GetUser `loading` means the list is emptied and the page shows the loading state on every mount (and any GetUser refetch) even when the user is already cached, because the watchQuery default is cache-and-network with notifyOnNetworkStatusChange. The role is already known from cache at that point, so this adds a network round trip of blank page for no reason.

The auto-select useEffect returns early when cohorts.length is 0, so a selectedCohortId set before every cohort emptied is never cleared. No test drives a coordinator from a selected cohort to zero visible cohorts (only 2-cohorts-to-1 is tested), so the stale id keeps the attendees query un-skipped for a cohort the coordinator can no longer see.

noVisibleCohorts guards on !cohortsLoading (and effectively !userLoading via the userData gate), but no test asserts it stays false while cohorts or the user are still loading — only the settled true/false cases are covered.

noVisibleCohorts explicitly guards on !cohortsLoading so the empty-state message cannot flash while the initial cohort page is still fetching, but no test asserts noVisibleCohorts stays false while cohortsLoading is true for a coordinator with an eventually-empty list.

userError is surfaced as the page error even when userData is already present (e.g. a cache-and-network GetUser refetch fails after the cached user loaded). The role is known in that case, yet the whole goals table is replaced by an error for a query this page only needs for one flag.

Which cohorts a coordinator may see is now a client-side rule inferred from trainingSize > 0, while the API already scopes that count per viewer. Any other consumer of newStaffCohorts (or a future one) must re-derive the same rule, and the schema says trainingSize excludes withdrawn households, so a cohort whose visible staff all withdrew also vanishes.
dismissalDetail: no thank you

message: The Monthly Gross Salary warning marker is rendered with focusable=false inside a CardActionArea that already has an explicit aria-label, so keyboard and screen-reader users tabbing through the report get no indication a staff member has this warning — only sighted mouse users who hover the red icon see it.

healthStatusLabel re-maps MpdHealthStatusEnum to the same four labels as the existing healthLabel in helpers.ts, differing only in case. That breaks the repo rule of one label per enum value: the two copies of the text can drift apart and add a second set of translation keys.

The legend hardcodes the fiscal-quarter month ranges as translated strings, although this same PR adds getQuarterMonthRange to helpers.ts to compute them. There are now two definitions of the fiscal calendar that can disagree.

The chip delete control is given role="button" and an aria-label but no tabIndex or onKeyDown, so assistive tech announces it as an actionable button that cannot actually be activated from the keyboard.

suppressErrors is applied to the whole ManagedStaff operation, but the report only renders staffError when the list is empty, so a failed load-more page (fetchMore, not caught) is now completely silent. It also skips reportGraphQLError in client.ts, so every non-FILTER_REQUIRED server error on this query stops reaching Rollbar/Datadog.

pageSize 100 assumes one page holds the whole result, but the API clamps `first` to 50 (MPDXSchema default_max_page_size 50; ManagedStaffQuery sets no max_page_size). For 51-100 staff, TeamSummary counts and spouse merging run over only the first 50 people until the user scrolls to trigger loadMore, so the summary cards show wrong per-team status counts.

grossSalaryWarning() and QuickGlance both evaluate only the primary staff member of a merged spouse row (member.quarterlyHealth, member.newStaffMonthlySalary come from the spread `...node`, never `partner`), so a merged partner whose own Monthly Gross Salary is below their own New Staff benchmark never triggers the warning or shows their own gross-salary figure.

t("{{count}} {{status}}", { count }) was added to translation.json as a bare key with no _one/_other suffixes, unlike every other count-driven key in this file. i18next will not find a pluralized form for this key, so the per-status count chip (e.g. "1 at risk") risks rendering the literal key or the wrong plural form, and yarn extract will re-split it into suffixed keys on the next run, silently dropping the flat key added here.

getLocalizedSecaStatus is a second SecaStatusEnum localizer; getLocalizedTaxStatus already exists and labels the same values differently ("Subject to SECA"/"Subject to FICA"/"Exempt" vs "Pays SECA"/"Pays FICA"/"Exempt from SECA"). HR staff now see two wordings for one enum value across HrTools.

The pendingField fallback branches in QuickGlance (empty departments array, null geographicLocation, null newStaffMonthlySalary) are new to this component and are never exercised: the only quick-glance test (StaffMember.test.tsx "shows the extra details when expanded") uses a fully-populated member fixture.

The team summary is derived from staffMembers, which is already filtered server-side by teamNames/search/department, so clicking a card collapses the strip to that team (plus partial counts for any other teams its members share). The cards cannot be used to switch team to team, and the "overview" changes with every unrelated filter.

useManagedStaffTeamsQuery() destructures only `data`, not `error`; a failed teams query silently returns teamCount = 0 and the whole Teams section disappears with no indication anything went wrong, even for a supervisor who genuinely has several teams.

QuickGlance.tsx calls t('Department') for the department label, but translation.json only has the pre-existing "Department: {{department}}" key, not a bare "Department" key — this diff omits the new key the mined i18n rule requires to be hand-added alongside its first t() call.

The summarizeTeams sort test only exercises the red- and yellow-count tiebreakers (Gamma/Beta/Alpha), never the final alphabetical tiebreak (`a.name.localeCompare(b.name)`) for two teams with equal red/yellow counts.

QuickGlance.tsx is a new non-trivial component (142 lines, formats currency/quarter/enum data) but has no colocated QuickGlance.test.tsx; its behavior is only exercised indirectly through StaffMember.test.tsx, so edge cases specific to QuickGlance (e.g. department de-duplication across partner teams, missing partner spouse fallback) have no direct unit coverage.

Unmerged-spouse name formatting (spouseFirstName + spouseLastName ?? lastName) is written twice, in QuickGlance.tsx:58 and StaffMember.tsx:104, while the other row-name rules live in helpers.ts (getRowName). A future change to spouse naming will have to find both copies.

Monthly Gross Salary below benchmark is flagged by coloring the value text `error.main` in addition to the existing GrossSalaryMarker icon+tooltip. The row view (StaffMember.tsx) only ever used the icon marker, never a red value, so this is a new, inconsistent way of signalling the same warning.
dismissalDetail: Matches the drawer, which already colours the value red beside the marker; UX retracted in debate

message: QuickGlance always renders a "Spouse" detail line when `partner` is set (merged row), duplicating the combined name already shown in the row header per the design spec ("Merged rows already carry both names"), but no test covers the merged-pair QuickGlance output to confirm or refute this.
The new error Alert has no retry action, so the only way to recover is a full page reload. The mined PR-history rule asks for an Alert with a retry affordance in place of the report.

The whole mocks object is now cast with `as ApolloErgonoMockMap`, so the typed GqlMockedProvider generic no longer checks the happy-path mockData in any test in this file. A misspelled or stale field in mockData would now compile and be silently ignored.

In supervisor view, a failed report leaves staffName undefined and dataLoading false, so AccountInfoBox renders an empty name line above the error Alert. It reads like a render bug next to the new error state.

The error branch is tested only as a dead end; no test covers recovery when the user picks another year from the header, which stays enabled in the error state. A change that latches the error (for example storing it in state) would leave the alert up forever and still pass.
The Try Again button has no disabled/loading guard, so a user can click it repeatedly while a refetch is in flight, firing overlapping requests.
dismissalDetail: loading never turns true during a refetch after an error, and Apollo already merges repeated clicks into the one request in flight

message: ExportCsvButton and the Print button stay enabled during reportError, letting the user export an empty CSV or print a blank report instead of being blocked like the sibling MPGA error-state PR did.
dismissalDetail: Export CSV and Print are not rendered when the query fails, since there is no data and so no transactions; returning to a loaded month is served from cache without a new request, so an error never appears next to old data

message: Both Salary Calculator useHcmQuery calls render HCM_UNAVAILABLE inline but do not pass suppressErrorCodes, so the global Apollo error link also toasts the raw API message ("HCM UserInfo report unavailable") on top of the alert, and again on every failed Try Again. This breaks the HrTools rule that a component rendering an error code itself must suppress that code.
dismissalDetail: kept the toast like #2108 so the HCM outage still reaches Datadog

message: The failed-retry test only asserts the button re-enables, which `.finally()` guarantees on its own, so deleting `.catch(() => {})` in handleRetry stays green while leaking an unhandled rejection. It also never checks that a second click calls refetch again, which is what the test name promises.
The new <Trans> string (Our records indicate... click "Request New MHA") has no matching entry in public/locales/en/translation.json, so the English catalog is missing the key.

isHcmApprovedOnly checks eligibility and approved amount on their own instead of per person, so an eligible user with no amount plus an ineligible spouse with an HCM amount shows the Board Approved card and hides the EligibilityStatusTable. The Salary Calculator already decides the same thing per person (useMhaRequestData: showUserFields = userEligible && userHasApprovedMha), so this is a second, looser rule for the same idea.

CurrentBoardApproved now has a hidden second mode (HCM-only) switched on by request === null, and the check is spread over about six spots (approved-on fallback, hidePrint, hideActions, two Last updated guards, two Approved on guards). A future caller that passes null for some other reason gets HCM dates and no actions without noticing.

The new per-person pairing is only tested on the spouse side; no test has an ineligible user with an HCM amount next to an eligible spouse with none. A change that pairs the user amount with eitherPersonEligible instead of userEligibleForMHA would still pass every test.

The positive anchor ("not applied" text from NoRequestsDisplay) does not depend on HCM data, so it can render before the Hcm query resolves and the negative assertion could pass before the user amount is ever seen. The local mutation check shows the two mocked queries settle together today, so this is a robustness gap, not a wrong test.
The removed t() strings have no remaining consumers but their keys stay in the English catalog. The repo rule says the orphaned key must be deleted in the same diff.

Only the ineligible-spouse half of the new HCM-only gating is tested; no test covers an ineligible user with an eligible, HCM-approved spouse. Mutating showUserRow to `true` or dropping `!userEligibleForMHA ||` from anyoneIneligible (MinisterHousingAllowance.tsx:133) leaves every test green.

After the first await findByText("Current Board Approved MHA"), the test awaits findByTestId("eligibility-status-table") even though the table renders in the same commit as the card (both gated on context already loaded), against the repo idiom of bare getBy* after the first findBy*.

usePdsSummaryData now requests constants for a goal's locked historical calculationsYear but never reads the hook's `unavailable` flag (returned when a year has no seeded constants), and no test exercises that branch. Before this PR the hook always requested the current year (effectively always available); locking to a goal's creation year makes 'no constants seeded for that year' a newly realistic path for older PDS goals with no test coverage or user-facing signal.

SetupStep.tsx and MonthlyReimbursableSection.tsx were changed to pass calculation?.calculationsYear into useGoalCalculatorConstants, but neither component's existing test file was updated to assert the GoalCalculatorConstants query is called with that year. Because the GqlMockedProvider mock for GoalCalculatorConstants is a static object (not variable-aware), a regression that silently drops or hardcodes the year argument in either file would not turn any test red.

The goal year is now passed by hand into three separate PDS calls to useGoalCalculatorConstants (SetupStep, MonthlyReimbursableSection, usePdsSummaryData). GoalCalculator does this differently: its context owns one year-scoped constants result and tells consumers not to call the hook themselves, so a future PDS consumer that calls the hook with no year will quietly get current-year rates.

The past-year comparison reads DateTime.local().year fresh on every render instead of capturing it once, unlike the repos established now = useMemo(() => DateTime.now(), []) pattern for long-lived pages. On a session left open across a year boundary the past-year banner/chip can appear or disappear mid-session even though nothing about the goal changed.

The new validator guard checks the sticky stableNonBackpayTotal (falls back to lastValidNonBackpayTotalRef), while useSalaryCalculations checks the live nonBackpayTotal, so the two exceedsCap answers split apart. An over-cap staffer who types a non-backpay amount and then clears it back to backpay-only sees "Optional Comments" and an enabled Submit, but Formik still fails additionalInfo as required.

`expect(calls.report).toBe(0)` can never fail: `calls.report` only increments inside `failCallsWhen`, and this test passes no `failReportCall`, so the counter is 0 even if the report query runs. The test does not prove the report query is skipped when HCM errors.

The non-array `graphQLErrors` guard is fixed only in the browser error link; the sibling SSR error link in src/lib/apollo/ssrClient.ts still calls `graphQLErrors.map(...)` behind a truthiness check, so a string or object `errors` throws inside the link the same way.

The new HCM failure path folds every Hcm error into the generic "Staff Expense report could not be loaded. Please try again later." alert, while the repo already has a dedicated convention for the Hcm query failing with HCM_UNAVAILABLE (isHcmUnavailableError + HcmUnavailableAlert). When HCM is overloaded, this page tells users something different from every other HCM-backed page.
dismissalDetail: it's no longer possible to get an HCM_UNAVAILABLE error on the Staff Expense Report except in an extreme edge case that isn't worth having special logic for

message: The reworded key "{{pending}} of {{total}} Pending" is not in public/locales/en/translation.json, and the diff has no catalog change.

The new sentence is missing the comma after the introductory phrase, and the trailing email has no ending punctuation, unlike the old copy that closed with a period. The bare address after a full sentence also reads as dangling rather than as part of the guidance.

The new no-restricted-syntax Trans selector is a fifth mechanically enforced i18n rule, but .claude/review/rules/standards.md still says "four rules ESLint enforces mechanically" and does not list the single-brace ban. Reviewers and agents reading that checklist will not know bare {expr} inside <Trans> is now a lint error.

The support link moved into a new SupportLink component, but LimitedAccess.test.tsx only checks the link by its name and never checks the mailto href. If the href broke during this refactor, all four cases would still pass.

Nothing in the jest suite can catch this bug class, because test i18n returns the key, so the English text looks right whether or not the key matches translation.json. The only guard is a complex esquery selector with no test, so a later edit could quietly turn it off and the bug would come back with every test still green.
dismissalDetail: lint rule covers it for now

message: The memoized schema local is named `EditAppealSchema` (PascalCase) while every other lane file uses a camelCase local like `taskSchema`. It reads like a component.
The yup test name is now t("Is positive?"), so it changes with the active language. No test checks that any of the 12 converted schemas uses the component t.
Yup test names no longer call t(), so the en keys "Is positive?" and "Is amount in valid currency format?" are orphaned. The repo rule says to delete orphaned keys with their last consumer.

The overlay only blocks the mouse, so keyboard users can still tab into the location autocomplete while the table is marked busy. Also, with cache-and-network and notifyOnNetworkStatusChange, hcmLoading turns true again on refetchHcm and dims the populated table.

The SECA note is now sourced from the hcmUser/hcmSpouse object (the separate Hcm query) while the dollar amount it annotates (calcs?.requestedSeca) comes from the independent SalaryCalculation query. If the two queries ever disagree on SECA status (stale draft calculation, HCM status corrected mid-session, in-flight refetch), the UI can render "has opted out of SECA" or "pays FICA instead of SECA" directly beside a non-zero SECA dollar figure.

The new "HCM has no SECA status on file ... the cap may be too low. Contact HR or Payroll to fix it" message is rendered as a plain <span className="explanation"> in theme.palette.text.secondary — visually identical to benign footnotes like the ASR backpay note on the same card. This tree already has an established pattern for HCM-data-missing warnings that affect a financial cap.
dismissalDetail: Author keeps the gray explanation style in this PR; the warning emphasis can be revisited in a follow-up PR if needed.

message: getSecaNote is a pure branching function (status + name + t -> string) but is unexported and only exercised indirectly through component render tests, not a direct unit test.

The shared hcmUserMock/hcmSpouseMock staffInfo blocks never set secaStatus, which was display-irrelevant before this PR but is now the sole driver of RequestSummaryCard's SECA note. Every other test that renders RequestSummaryCard through this shared wrapper now shows an unintended, unasserted SECA note.

getSecaNote re-lists SecaStatusEnum (Fica/Seca/Optout) in a second switch in this file, independently of src/components/HrTools/Shared/getLocalizedTaxStatus.tsx, which switches on the same three members. The two helpers legitimately diverge in output shape though: getLocalizedTaxStatus returns a compact chip label and returns undefined for a missing status; getSecaNote returns full name-interpolated sentences plus a 4th branch (an actionable HR/Payroll warning) that getLocalizedTaxStatus has no equivalent for. Revised per round-1 debate (UX, Testing): the duplication risk is real but narrow (if the enum grows, both switches need a new case), not a correctness or test-debt issue, since neither helper's sentence templates could be eliminated by delegation.
dismissalDetail: The chip label helper and the sentence note are kept as separate presentations on purpose; a shared label map for three strings is not worth the indirection here.

message: The "keeps going when a step throws" test only asserts localStorage was cleared, so it cannot catch a regression where a failing clearStore or caches.keys stops later steps. It also never covers a throwing clearDatadogUser or one rejected caches.delete.

The clear-then-sign-out sequence is now copied by hand into five call sites (logout page, ProfileMenu, ProfileMenuPanel, ConnectOrganization, Apollo error link). The next sign-out path someone adds can call next-auth signOut directly and skip clearing cached donor data, and nothing will catch it.
Redundant beforeEach mockClear in both impersonation accordion tests (Admin :266, Organization :130): jest.config.js already sets clearMocks: true.

shouldKeepOnSignOut is tested with hand-written cache names, and nothing ties them to the name Serwist builds from cacheId. If cacheId or the prefix drifts, precache is wiped on sign-out or runtime caches survive, and no test goes red.

`attempt` swallows every failure with no logging, so if Cache Storage or the Apollo store fails to clear on sign-out or impersonation start, the team never finds out. That is exactly the privacy guarantee this PR is meant to provide.

The IndexedDB connection is cached forever, so once it closes (the blocking handler closes it, or the browser drops it, as Safari does after backgrounding) every later clear() throws. Sign-out purge then fails and the signed-out user's cached data stays on disk until the next sign-in clears it.

Setting maxSize: false means the whole normalized cache (including HR, salary and MHA data) now stays on disk, where the old 1MB localStorage limit used to purge large caches. When a session ends by token expiry instead of signOutAndClear, nothing purges IndexedDB, so that data stays readable on a shared machine until the next sign-in.
dismissalDetail: needed for offline support

message: Keeping the server HTML while CacheRestoreGate suspends depends on an unwritten rule: nothing above the Suspense boundary may change context during hydration. Only comments and React.memo enforce it, and no test covers it, even though it already broke twice in this PR (commits 393c6c928, a0e9c709c).

The query only reads data and ignores error, so if GetDefaultAccount fails (offline or API error) the user sees the full-page spinner forever on /accountLists/_/... URLs. Only a transient toast explains it, and there is no retry or fallback.

The "_" account list rule now lives in two places that disagree. The server handleUnderscoreAccountListRedirect does nothing when there is no default account list, but the new client version sends the user to /accountLists. The same URL acts differently depending on whether the page has getServerSideProps.
The same module is imported twice (namespace and default), which can trip import/no-duplicates and is needless.

Moving minWidth: 700 into a breakpoint media query beats the ChartFrame consumer override `sx={{ minWidth: 0 }}` at md and up, so MPGA chart loading boxes now get forced to 700px on desktop. Before this PR the plain sx declaration won over the plain base declaration.
The same fixed 700px min-width empty/loading box exists in local copies that this PR leaves alone, so those screens still overflow on phones. Without a follow-up, the fix only covers part of the app.
The new maxWidth and overflowWrap were added to an inline style prop, which the UX rules forbid (bypasses theme).
HeaderBarContactWrap is flex:1 without minWidth:0, so a very long unbroken contact name could still widen the header row at 390px.

The new below-sm branch (Add Person rendered after the people list) has no test. ContactDetailsTabPeople.test.tsx never mocks matchMedia, so jsdom always takes the desktop path and the mobile placement is unexercised.

On platforms with classic (non-overlay) scrollbars, a narrow window shows a ~15px horizontal scrollbar inside the fixed 48px row. The button content is 48px tall (32px plus 8px margins), so the scrollbar can clip the bottom of the buttons.
New hook under src/components has no colocated test, and no existing test covers its phone-closed or desktop-open behavior across the six providers that now use it.

The responsive calc(100vh - nav - header - appealHeader) height is now duplicated in ContactsList and ContactFlowColumn (the latter with an extra 87px), each hand-pairing the mobile and desktop constants.
dismissalDetail: the header responsive calc is dependent on individual screen layouts, there is no need to try and make a common function

message: The new `isNarrow && !isEmpty` guard has no test for the empty state on phones, so dropping `!isEmpty` would not fail any test.
The trigger button icon (which reflects the current view) is never asserted, and the menu closing after a selection is not checked, so breaking either would stay green.
useMediaQuery runs without noSsr, so the first render is always the desktop toolbar and phones flash the wide toggle group before swapping to the menu button.
The view list (value, label, icon) is defined in mobileViewOptions and again by hand in the desktop ToggleButtons, so adding a view means editing two places.
Every row in mockData has lastReminder: null, so the new Last Reminder stacked line is only ever tested as absent. Deleting the Typography or flipping its guard would not turn the test red.

The test name claims stacking happens on phones, but jsdom does not apply the responsive display rules and getByText ignores visibility, so the test passes at any width and does not check the hide/show behavior.
The new test uses a `!` non-null assertion on `cells.find(...)`, which fails with an unclear TypeError if the partner row is missing.

RemindersTableRow now imports a runtime value (hideOnPhone) from RemindersTable, which itself imports RemindersTableRow, turning a type-only back-reference into a real circular module dependency. It works today only because hideOnPhone is read at render time, so a future module-level use (e.g. a styled() call or default prop) would see undefined.
New shared component ScrollableTableContainer has no colocated test. The repo checklist requires a Foo.test.tsx next to every new non-trivial component.

ScrollHint (styled Typography, hidden above sm, flex with SwipeIcon) is a copy of the ScrollHint already in Reports/FourteenMonthReports/Layout/Table/Table.tsx, along with the same sticky first-column and 8px cell padding idea. Two copies of the phone scroll hint will drift (the report one already has a print rule this one lacks).
dismissalDetail: duplicate of 1

message: The test only checks the hint text and a cell exist. jsdom ignores the media queries, so deleting the pinned column, padding, or the below-sm hint display rule keeps it green.
dismissalDetail: jsdom can't test layout or media queries, checked in the browser

message: barSize to maxBarSize and the removed minWidth/overflow change chart layout with no test; the existing MonthlyCommitment tests cannot detect a regression.
dismissalDetail: jsdom can't test layout or media queries, checked in the browser

message: The phone padding removal sits on the shared ToolsGridContainer, so it also changes ToolsHome, MergeContacts, MergePeople, GoogleImport, TntConnect and CsvImportWrapper, not just the Fix tools the PR names. Repo rules ask that a shared-style edit list every consumer and say whether each was meant to change.
dismissalDetail: PR body already lists every ToolsGridContainer consumer as intended, and PageContentWrapper keeps a 16px gutter so nothing touches the screen edge

message: The flex-column Form wrapper is local to AddDonation, but sibling Modal dialogs that put DialogContent inside a plain Formik Form (CreateMultipleContacts, SettingsDialog) have the same non-scrolling-footer layout and are left unfixed.

The hidden-state tests assert absence right after the request is made, before the mocked response resolves. The card is also hidden while data is loading, so these tests pass even if the hiding logic is broken.

Several added comments run 3 lines (the calculations and newStaffCohortAttendee comments here, plus the comment blocks in Dashboard.test.tsx), against the project rule of 1 line, 2 at most. This is convention drift only.

The NS Goal Calculator access gate (reportsDisabled || DISABLE_NS_GOAL_CALCULATOR || inNsGoalCalcIneligibleGroup) is now copied by hand from useHrToolsNavItems, and the comment says the card must match the menu. If the menu gate changes, nothing keeps the card in sync and it can link to a page the user cannot open.

The card treats any returned newStaffGoalCalculation as proof the goal was sent, and its only send check (newStaffCohortAttendee.goalSentAt) is skipped precisely when the attendee is null, which the diff says is the staff member's own case. If the API returns a pre-send calculation to the staff member, they are told "Your MPD goal is ready" and pointed at a draft goal.
dismissalDetail: the API's own-account read (NewStaffGoalScoped#own_sent_account_list_goals) only returns a staff member's goal after it is sent; the attendee check covers the goals-team path

message: The acknowledgement re-implements src/hooks/useUserPreference (query + mutation + optimisticResponse + a local `dismissed` mirror) instead of wrapping it, giving the repo a second way to read and write a user option.
dismissalDetail: useUserPreference applies the loaded value a frame late and flashes the card; reading the option query directly avoids that

message: useNewStaffGoalReadyQuery destructures only data, so a query error is indistinguishable from a legitimately absent goal and the card silently disappears with no retry path or logged signal beyond the generic Apollo toast.
dismissalDetail: hiding a promo card on a lookup error is the intended fallback and is covered by a test

message: The renamed Send Status column header and the Ready to Send / Not Ready chip text have no rendered assertion in GoalsTable.test.tsx. Reverting the header or chip labels in the table would not fail any test.

The new doc says isCalculationComplete must match the API REQUIRED_FOR_SEND lists, but the API list (mpdx_api#3720) also requires first_name, last_name and geographic_location, which this helper never checks. The same rule now lives in two repos kept in sync only by cross-referencing comments, and the comments already overstate the match.
"Goal Status" is orphaned after GoalsTable switched to "Send Status" and ScenarioGoals to "Calculation Status".

New keys were hand-added but the now-unused keys (Goal Status, Run and Send All/Selected Complete MPD Goals?) were left behind, so the file no longer matches what yarn extract produces. Stale keys get pushed to CrowdIn and translated for nothing.
The handleSend branch that commits a typed-but-uncommitted address and then bails when it is invalid or exceeds the max has no test.
SendScenarioGoalDialog is statically imported and always mounted, so its Autocomplete form code ships in the initial bundle instead of using the Dynamic<Name> pattern.
While sending, the form is swapped for a bare spinner with no text or status role, so screen reader users get no announcement and the dialog height jumps.
The in-flight guard (Cancel/backdrop disabled while sending) and chip removal via onChange are untested.

The client regex is described as a port of email_validator :strict, but swapping Ruby [[:alpha:]]/[[:alnum:]] for \p{L}/\p{N} makes the two disagree on some Unicode input. The server re-validates, so the impact is limited to a few exotic addresses: some pass in the browser and then fail on send (with a toast, dialog stays open), and some valid ones are blocked in the browser.
New tests `await userEvent.click/type`, but the pinned user-event v13 is synchronous so the await does nothing.

The empty-sentTo branch can no longer happen: the client always sends at least one address, and the API now raises on an empty list and otherwise returns the validated recipients. The new copy "No email addresses were given" describes a case that ends in an error toast, not this branch.

The in-flight guards (guardedClose, Cancel disabled while sending, spinner swap) are new behavior with no test, so removing them keeps every test green. The new component also has no colocated SendScenarioGoalDialog.test.tsx and is only exercised through the hook test.

The dialog hand-rolls form state, touched tracking and validation with useState plus a yup schema run through isValidSync, while HrTools CLAUDE.md names Formik/Yup as the form convention. Similar single-email forms (InviteForm, ImpersonateUserAccordion) use Formik with yup.string().email().required().

While sending, the focused email TextField is unmounted and swapped for a spinner, so keyboard focus drops to the dialog container and nothing announces the busy state. On a failed send the field remounts and autoFocus fires again.

SendableScenarioGoal dropped emailAddress/spouseEmailAddress, but ScenarioGoals.graphql still fetches both under a comment saying they drive the send recipient list and disabled reason. The query now pulls two unused fields with a comment that is false.
New tests `await userEvent.click/type`, but the repo pins user-event v13 where these are synchronous, so the await does nothing.
The failure test builds its own ThemeProvider and GqlMockedProvider and casts mocks with `as ApolloErgonoMockMap`, bypassing the typed GqlMockedProvider generic idiom.

The new print-click test duplicates the PrintGoalControls and PresentingYourGoalStep click tests, so it only proves wiring that the shared test already covers. The print-hidden additions on the intro text and the Continue button have no test.
printSpy.mockRestore() runs after the assertion, so a failing expect leaves window.print stubbed for later tests (jest config has clearMocks but not restoreMocks).

The new helper text says the spouse pre-fill is a net-salary estimate, but the API still pre-fills gross salary. If this ships before the MPDX-10258 API change, senior-staff spouses are told a gross number is their take-home pay.
dismissalDetail: the PR body states the MPDX-10258 API dependency and this PR must not merge before it

message: Two new translation keys say the same HCM-estimate thing in different words ("{{spouseName}}`s pre-filled amount is an estimate from their current HCM salary" vs "The pre-filled amount is an estimate from {{spouseName}}`s current HCM salary"). Translators get two strings for one idea and the wording can drift later.
The reworded validation message "Please enter the city of your assignment" has no test, so a wrong or dropped message would not turn any test red.

The new test asserts the Formik validation message with a synchronous getByText right after userEvent.tab(), but Formik runs blur validation asynchronously. The test is likely to fail or be flaky, and the bare .focus() call runs outside act.

PartnersSection uses alignItems: center, so each PartnerSection is vertically centered on its own height; when labels wrap to different line counts (e.g. Special Gift Partners vs Prayer Partners at 390px), the three numbers sit at different heights.

No test pins `context: { suppressErrorCodes: [MHA_WOULD_END_CODE] }` on the submit call. Dropping it would show the global error toast on top of the warning dialog and every new test would stay green.

The 'leaves out the paycheck date' test asserts the fallback text right after the PayrollDates call is seen, which is also the loading state. It can pass before the response arrives, so a bug that wrongly matches a date would not fail it.
No test asserts the submit sends context.suppressErrorCodes ['MHA_WOULD_END'], so dropping that line would show a raw toast over the warning with every test still green.

The warning derives the paycheck date from the client's cached calculation.effectiveDate instead of the effectiveDate the server put in the error, so a stale cache can show a different date than the server checked.
The warning joins two translated sentences with a hard-coded leading space, so translators cannot reorder them and spaceless locales get a stray space.
The new catch returns silently for every non-MHA error, so submit failures no longer reach Rollbar as unhandled rejections and a non-Apollo error gives the user no feedback.

When the API rejects with MHA_WOULD_END, the open dialog swaps its title, body, and adds a required checkbox in place with no announcement, so screen reader users may not learn the submit was blocked.
The new string says 'Ministry Housing Allowance (MHA)' while all 18 other strings in the app say 'Minister's Housing Allowance', the tax term.
SubmitModal's acknowledged state never resets when the acknowledgement prop changes, so a future caller that swaps the label while the modal stays open would keep a stale check.
When the dialog switches to the MHA warning, the focused confirm button becomes disabled and nothing announces the new content or the required checkbox to screen-reader users.

The required typescript check fails because the production schema CI generates from has no confirmMhaEnd on SalaryRequestSubmitMutationInput. The PR cannot merge until mpdx_api#3770 is live in production.
dismissalDetail: CI builds types and mocks from the prod API schema, which gets confirmMhaEnd when mpdx_api 3770 deploys, so these pass once the API ships first

message: The new 'resubmits with confirmMhaEnd once confirmed, then advances' test fails in CI because the production-derived mock schema rejects the unknown confirmMhaEnd input.
dismissalDetail: CI builds types and mocks from the prod API schema, which gets confirmMhaEnd when mpdx_api 3770 deploys, so these pass once the API ships first

message: Because this PR compiles only against an API that already has confirmMhaEnd, the API must deploy first, leaving a window where the old frontend gets MHA_WOULD_END with no way to confirm. Staff ending MHA see a raw toast until this PR ships.
dismissalDetail: the API deploys first on purpose, and until this front end ships a refused submit shows a plain error and nothing ends, which is the safe failure

message: confirmMhaEnd is a bare boolean, so the server skips the whole check on resubmit even if the set of people losing MHA changed after the warning. MHA could end for someone the dialog never named.
dismissalDetail: matches the API's dismissed finding 4, the confirm covers one submit and the warning lists everyone the request ends MHA for

message: When extensions.people is missing or no entry passes isMhaEndPerson, MhaEndWarning renders nothing, so the user confirms ending MHA without seeing whose or when. The server message that names them is discarded because the toast is suppressed.
dismissalDetail: the API always sends each person's name and number, and the dialog title and body still say MHA will stop

message: The MHA branch returns before the progressive-approval branch, so a request that needs extra approval loses its 'may affect your selected effective date' note on the confirm screen.
dismissalDetail: the user already saw the progressive approval note in the first submit dialog before the MHA warning replaced it

message: handleSubmit now rethrows every non-MHA_WOULD_END error, but SubmitModal wires it straight to a Button onClick with no catch. A failed submit now also raises an unhandled promise rejection on top of the global error toast.
dismissalDetail: this restores how submit behaved before the PR, where a failed submit reached Rollbar as an unhandled rejection, which finding 11 asked for

message: isMhaEndPerson drops a person whose reason is null or missing, though the MhaEndPerson doc says a person with an unknown reason is still listed.
dismissalDetail: the API always sends a reason string for every person

message: Two new warningText branches have no test: NoHousingType without a paycheck date, and an unknown reason with a paycheck date. A swapped or mistyped string in either would stay green.
dismissalDetail: those two branches use the same translation pattern the other four tests cover

message: The acknowledgement checkbox resets only when the label text changes, so a second MHA_WOULD_END with a different people list would keep the box checked.
dismissalDetail: a resubmit carries confirmMhaEnd true, so the server cannot answer it with a second MHA_WOULD_END

message: The required checkbox stays enabled while submitting, so the user can uncheck it during a request that already carries confirmMhaEnd: true.
dismissalDetail: unchecking during an in-flight submit cannot change the request already sent

message: The test adds one key with addResource but afterEach removes the whole English bundle, so setup and teardown do not match.
dismissalDetail: the test removes the bundle it changed, and every test file starts with a fresh bundle

message: MhaEndWarning mounts another PayrollDates query, which under the cache-and-network default makes one more network request each time the warning appears.
dismissalDetail: PayrollDates is usually cached from the effective date step, and one extra request when the warning appears is cheap

message: useSubmitDialogContent now returns early with MHA content that ignores its other inputs, so one hook serves two unrelated dialogs.
dismissalDetail: the hook already picks dialog content by state, and the MHA warning is one more state

message: The PR template checklist still tells authors to run `/quality:agent-review`, a stale command name from the same agent-review move this PR cleans up.
formatAmount uses currencyFormat's default stripIfInteger, so the right-aligned money column mixes whole dollars and cents.
The print table reads saved cache values, so an edit still being typed (lump-sum field before blur, grid cell in edit mode) is missing from a Ctrl+P printout.
dismissalDetail: The print table shows saved values. Capturing an edit still being typed is a follow-up outside this PR's scope.

message: No test covers the branch where goalCalculation has not loaded, so the goal name and names lines are skipped. Removing the `goalCalculation &&` guard would not fail any test.
dismissalDetail: The goal-not-loaded branch only skips the name lines. A test for it is a small follow-up, scope frozen for this PR.

message: A local formatAmount duplicates useFormatters().formatCurrency, which HrTools CLAUDE.md asks new code to prefer.
dismissalDetail: Moving to useFormatters().formatCurrency is a follow-up. The local helper keeps the print formatting in one place.

message: The total row border uses a raw 'black' literal and raw '2px' instead of a theme token.
dismissalDetail: Same finding as #6, already dismissed.

message: While the goal loads, the screen content is screen-only and the print table is not mounted, so Ctrl+P prints a blank page.
dismissalDetail: The Print button is disabled until the goal loads. A blank Ctrl+P during the brief load is a follow-up, scope frozen for this PR.

message: The salary export passes each table's group currency (the donor currency key of currencyGroups) as the report currency, but in Salary mode every month.total is already converted to the salary currency. For a non-salary group (e.g. CAD with USD salary) a CAD pledge is treated as already in report currency, so the CAD commitment is capped against USD in-hand amounts and summed into the USD total.

The mixed-currency skip in getGiftConversionRate (months where any gift is not in the commitment currency are left out of the rate) has no test. Deleting that `donations.some(...)` guard keeps every spec green.

getSolidMonthlySupport takes a generic currency argument, but getGiftConversionRate always derives a rate to the salary currency from salaryCurrencyTotal while the in-hand side sums month.total. The pair only agrees when month.total is itself the salary-converted total, which is true in salary mode only, so a future caller in partner currency mode gets a commitment converted to the wrong currency.
The new useMemo calls t() but its dependency list omits t, so the label will not update when the language changes (react-hooks/exhaustive-deps).
useCsvData now imports the FourteenMonthReportCurrencyType enum as a value from FourteenMonthReport.tsx, which itself imports useCsvData, creating a runtime import cycle.
dismissalDetail: useFourteenMonthReport.ts already value-imports the same enum from FourteenMonthReport.tsx, and it is read only when the hook runs

message: The switch from salaryCurrencyTotal to total in getGiftConversionRate is not pinned by any test. Reverting it keeps every spec green.
dismissalDetail: on the Salary Currency report, the only place this runs, useFourteenMonthReport.ts sets month.total to salaryCurrencyTotal, so the two are equal by construction

message: Each per-table row passes the donor-currency group key as the report currency, but in salary mode month.total is already salary-converted. For a CAD group with a CAD pledge, getCommittedInCurrency returns the raw CAD commitment while inHand sums USD-converted totals, so the row is mixed-currency and labeled CAD.
dismissalDetail: in salary mode the API groups gifts by Donation#converted_currency, the designation account currency, and converted_amount is in that same currency, so each table's totals are in its key currency

message: The CAD row only asserts 0, so it passes if each row reused the wrong table's contacts or currency in the calculation. Only the label and currency column are really checked.
dismissalDetail: the per-contact math is tested in monthlyEquivalents.test.ts, and a nonzero CAD row would rewrite the shared full-export fixture

message: The coordinator gating tests assert before GetUser resolves, when isGoalsAdmin is false for everyone, so they never check a loaded coordinator.

When the coach list query fails, options is empty, so the picker says "No MPD coaches have been added yet". That is a false claim about the data and sends the user to an admin tab instead of showing a failure.

The 'adds the picked person and closes' test only checks the mutation variables and handleClose. Dropping refetchQueries or update: evictCoachLists from the modal would leave it green, so a newly added coach could stay missing from the list and the pickers.
dismissalDetail: evictCoachLists has its own cache tests and the update hook is one line

message: The MPD Coaches table shows listed coaches who are no longer assignable with no marker, under a header saying these are the coaches you can assign. They silently vanish from the Assign Coach pickers.
dismissalDetail: a coach who left Cru stays on the tab until removed and drops out of the picker, a known follow-up from mpdx_api#3784

message: The empty-picker alert says no MPD coaches have been added, but the picker list is also empty when every listed coach has become ineligible. The admin then sees coaches on the MPD Coaches tab and a message that contradicts it.
dismissalDetail: a coach who left Cru stays on the tab until removed and drops out of the picker, a known follow-up from mpdx_api#3784

message: searchFor waits on real timers for a 500ms debounce inside waitFor's default 1000ms timeout, leaving only a 500ms margin on a loaded CI shard. This can make several tests flaky.
dismissalDetail: the debounced search tests pass on repeated local runs, no flake seen

message: Tests keep the whole render result in `utils` and call `utils.findByRole` instead of destructuring queries from `render()`, which is the repo idiom.
dismissalDetail: the utils object keeps the shared searchFor helper simple

message: evictCoachLists evicts the modal's own watched candidates query on a successful add, so Apollo refetches the current search right before the modal closes.
dismissalDetail: the refetch keeps the listed flags right if the modal stays open

message: The inline add-failure alert duplicates the global error toast, against the MpdGoalAdmin note in HrTools CLAUDE.md that mutation failures toast through the global link.
dismissalDetail: the modal stays open on failure, so it needs its own message beside the toast

message: onInputChange stores MUI's 'reset' value after a pick, so each pick fires a second debounced HCM search for the picked name.
dismissalDetail: one extra small search after a pick

message: After a pick the input shows only the name, so with two same-name candidates the admin cannot confirm which one Save will add.
dismissalDetail: department and person number show in the option list before the pick

message: No test covers the loading spinner, or the 'failed background refetch keeps the loaded table' branch (error && !data). Flipping that guard would pass every test.
dismissalDetail: loading spinner and background-refetch tests are a follow-up

message: The coordinator fallback for ?tab=mpd-coaches is applied in the view, so the context's activeTab still reports mpd-coaches for users who cannot see it.
dismissalDetail: the coordinator fallback sits where the tab renders, as planned

message: coach.options includes the seeded assigned coach, so when the MPD list is empty but a coach is assigned the field says 'No coaches match your search.' instead of pointing to the MPD Coaches tab.
Comments still describe the OneApp contract ('costs an OneApp lookup', 'Eligibility can't change while the page is open') though the list is now admin-managed.
Options are gated on the debounced search, so clearing the input keeps showing the old results for up to 500ms.
dismissalDetail: old results for up to 500ms while clearing are harmless

message: The remove update builds the cache id by hand instead of cache.identify, which would quietly miss if NewStaffMpdCoach ever got custom keyFields.
dismissalDetail: NewStaffMpdCoach uses default keyFields

message: Adds a 'Remove {{name}}' translation key when 'Remove {{label}}' already exists with the same English.
